kind.zh: 臺語 AI 音樂錄影帶。手作布偶與微縮場景。
kind.en: Music video, Taiwanese song. Handmade puppets and miniature sets.

en: “The Wind of Cijin”, lyrics by Punkcan, music by Suno

zh: 一顆海螺，從三百多年前漂到旗後沙洲的漁人手上開始，一代傳過一代：天后宮前的孩子、天還沒亮就坐頭班船去上工的阿母、看著沙洲被挖開成港口的一家人，一直到今天把海螺貼在耳邊的孫子。
這支片用手作布偶和微縮場景的質感，配上我寫詞的臺語歌〈旗津的風〉，把旗津從沙洲半島變成島、又被過港隧道連回高雄的這條路，重新走一遍。
把海螺貼在耳邊，聽見的不只是海。
en: A conch shell passes from hand to hand for more than three hundred years: from a fisherman blown ashore on the Cihou sandbar, to a child outside the Mazu temple, to a mother taking the first ferry across before dawn, to a family watching the sandbar dug open for a harbor, and finally to a grandchild holding it to his ear today.

Told with handmade puppets and miniature sets, and set to “The Wind of Cijin,” a Taiwanese song I wrote the lyrics for, the film walks again the road Cijin has travelled: from a sandbar peninsula, to an island, to being joined back to Kaohsiung by the Cross-Harbor Tunnel.
Hold a conch to your ear, and you hear more than the sea.

zh: 紅毛港，跟旗津一樣都是我的故鄉，也是我童年的所在。
2007 年，延遲了三十幾年的紅毛港全村遷離，那片海岸成了貨櫃碼頭，小時候熟悉的巷子和海，從此只能在記憶裡找。
這也是我想做這支片的原因：既然回不去了，就用 AI 把它重新蓋起來。
選了紙藝的畫風，一摺一摺地，把烏魚季的海、門口補網的身影、越住越擠的老屋，一直到搬家的那一天，重新搭起來。
這也是我第一支完成度較高的 AI 影片。
從劇本、分鏡，到一鏡一鏡生成、剪接，再配上臺語歌〈網的這一頭〉和字幕，每個細節用我目前最初淺的AI影片技能去慢慢地磨琢。
那張補了又補、最後交到女兒手上的漁網，我想是有些東西還是會一代一代被接住。
en: Hongmaogang is my hometown, the place where I grew up.

In 2007, after more than thirty years of delay, the entire village of Hongmaogang was relocated, and its shoreline became a container terminal. The lanes and the sea I knew as a child now live only in memory.
That is why I made this film: if I can't go back, I can rebuild it with AI.

I chose a papercraft style, folding it back together piece by piece — the sea in mullet season, the figures mending nets at the door, the old houses growing ever more crowded, all the way to moving day.
This is my first fairly complete AI film.

From script and storyboard to generating and editing shot by shot, then adding the Taiwanese song “This End of the Net” and subtitles, I worked through every detail with the modest AI filmmaking skills I have so far.
The fishing net, mended again and again until it is finally handed to the daughter — I believe some things are still caught and carried on, generation after generation.
